customManagers.description: hk.pkl imports hk's Pkl schema and builtins from a release, which should match the hk pinned in mise.toml.
Homebrew/actions tags have four parts (2026.11.02.1), which the github-actions manager truncates to three and then cannot find, so this manager reads the full tag.

packageRules.description: The Homebrew/actions custom manager above owns these pins; the built-in manager would only raise its truncated-tag warning.

@types/node tracks the engines floor, not the newest DefinitelyTyped release or the Node that dev and CI run: types from a later major describe APIs the oldest supported Node lacks, and tsc believes them. Move the ceiling when the floor moves.
Pi paste declares a Node 22 floor.
Pi's extension loader swaps in the typebox it bundles, so pi-paste pins that exact version by hand and realigns it when Pi moves.
pi-paste tests against Pi releases as they ship without raising the supported floor for in-range releases.

Pi's docs/packages.md has a package declare the packages Pi provides as peerDependencies at "*", so it loads in whichever Pi hosts it. Renovate leaves those peers alone; the devDependencies carry the Pi the package is built against.

mise installs Biome from GitHub through aqua, whose registry reads its @biomejs/biome@X.Y.Z tags with a version_filter Renovate cannot see (Renovate's mise manager docs), so the version is extracted here.

mise generates the files under .mise/locks when it locks a tool, and Renovate's mise manager regenerates them with each bump. Left on, the npm manager also reads the npm-renovate sidecar's package.json and bumps it alone, out of step with its aube-lock.yaml and mise.renovate.lock's digest

biome.json's $schema names the exact Biome release, kept current by customManagers:biomeVersions, so Biome is pinned exactly as its install guide does (npm i -E) and the package, the schema, and any mise pin move in one PR. Last, so it overrides the per-manager groups.
